questions.question: What is true about Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: Most trucks do not have them.
They are not useful in most situations.

questions.explanation: Since 1997-1999, most commercial trucks, trailers, and dollies must have ABS.

questions.question: When you start from a complete stop, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must not roll backwards when you start from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: If cargo leaks during transport, how should you identify the hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Use the shipping papers, labels, or package location to identify leaking materials. Never touch or smell them—this could cause injury or death.

questions.question: In wet conditions, if other vehicles are not spraying water from their tires, this means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is trapped under the vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, a lack of tire spray means ice has formed on the road. Drive extra carefully in wet, freezing weather.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes to the report.
Check the report first when starting your inspection.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the report first when starting your inspection.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reading any report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Push the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What is true about carrying liquids in a leaking tank?

options.text: It is okay if no one is following you.
It is safe as long as there are no sparks.

questions.explanation: Before driving a tank vehicle, check for cracks or leaks. It is illegal to carry liquids or gases in a leaking tank.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights and flashers. Do not use high beams—they reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Explosives are classified as Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which of these is NOT a concern?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: Check tires for proper tread depth (at least 4/32 inch on front tires and 2/32 inch on other tires), wear, cracks, and correct air pressure. All tires should be the same size. Different manufacturers are not a concern.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave it right away and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts at the crossing. Call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should be no more than:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for correctly labeling and marking hazardous materials. The driver should check that the shipper labeled and marked everything properly before starting the trip.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should:
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must not leak or be broken. A broken exhaust system allows poisonous fumes to enter the cab.

questions.question: A vehicle without proper placards:

options.text: May only be moved in an emergency.
May be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: May only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for hazardous materials may not be driven, except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Easy to see when entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see when entering the cab.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous materials, keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or another place you can easily reach while wearing your seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When driving in hot weather:

options.text: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, air pressure increases as air expands, so check your tire pressure often. To prevent overheating, keep enough oil in the engine and enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system. Antifreeze helps in both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: If a parked trailer has no spring brakes, you should prevent it from moving by:

options.text: Parking it against a wall or another vehicle.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from moving.

questions.question: If you drive slowly and block traffic, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: When starting from a stop:

options.text: A vehicle should shift to the right.
A vehicle should go into third gear.
A vehicle should not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle should not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.
